title: KV cache SLAs: traffic-scenario fuzzer and regression alerting
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Build a traffic-scenario fuzzer and associated alerting to validate KV/prefix cache behavior across realistic traffic mixes. Goal: exercise hit-rate vs p95 vs memory trade-offs and catch regressions that reduce tokens/sec or increase tail latency under mixed workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Fuzzer can generate at least three traffic archetypes: conversational (long context, high prefix reuse), short-query (many unique prefixes), and mixed-burst (bursts of long/short).
Test harness yields stable, repeatable metrics (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, cache hit-rate, resident memory).
Automated regression detector flags a run when p95 increases >20% or tokens/sec drops >15% compared to baseline for the same scenario, and posts a Slack alert with link to detailed artifacts.
Results are viewable in Grafana dashboard with automated annotations for failing runs and links to failing PRs.
Run matrix completes under CI budget (<4 hours for full sweep), and can be narrowed to smoke tests for quick pre-merge checks.
test_plan: Implement 'scenario fuzzer' binary in load-tests repo that replays synthetic client groups with configurable prefix reuse distributions and sequence-length histograms.
Create baseline corpora: conv-100k, short-1m, mixed-250k derived from anonymized production prompts (privacy reviewed).
Parameterize runs: concurrency, tokens/sec target, KV cache size (GB), eviction policy, prefix prefetch ratio.
Capture metrics via existing runtime telemetry tags: kv.hits, kv.misses, tokens.generated, request.latency.ms (per-quantile), process.resident_bytes.
Add a 'regression-detector' step that compares current run to stored baseline snapshots and returns non-zero exit on threshold breach.
Integrate smoke mode in GitHub Actions for quick checks and a nightly full-sweep job in CircleCI with artifact retention.
progress_updates: 2025-02-13: Kickoff with infra and telemetry. Agreed on required labels (kv.hits, request.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, resident_bytes).
2025-02-18: Prototype fuzzer implemented (load-tests/fuzzer-v0) that supports variable prefix-reuse ratios. Initial runs against local dev cluster completed.
2025-02-21: Memory accounting mismatch discovered: resident_bytes reported by the runtime excludes slab allocator free lists. Filed follow-up ENG-27945 to reconcile allocator accounting.
2025-02-24: Baseline capture process defined; saving run snapshots with deterministic seed and scenario metadata to S3 (s3://redwood-perf/kv-fuzzer/baselines/).
2025-02-27: Regression detector prototype compares p95 and tokens/sec to baseline and pushes a GitHub check with diff summary. Hooked into PR CI for candidate PRs changing cache logic.
2025-03-01: Nightly sweep scheduled and Grafana dashboard panel created. Still tuning alert thresholds to balance noise vs sensitivity.
decisions: Use three canonical scenarios (conversational, short-query, mixed-burst) rather than attempting to emulate every customer profile.
Alert thresholds: p95 +20% and tokens/sec -15% relative to baseline for a fail; reason: protects both latency and throughput SLAs.
Store baselines per runtime release (release-tag) to avoid false positives when intentional changes land; regression detector compares within same release bucket by default.
Prefetch parameter default will be 0.2 (20% prefetch) for mixed-burst scenarios; we can sweep this in experiments but tests default to that value for CI consistency.
test_runs: 2025-02-20 dev-cluster conv-10k: baseline tokens/sec 24k, p95 42ms, kv.hit-rate 78%
2025-02-22 dev-cluster short-50k: baseline tokens/sec 45k, p95 18ms, kv.hit-rate 21%
2025-02-26 mixed-burst-nightly: noticed 28% p95 regression when prefetch enabled with small cache sizes (replicable).
2025-02-28 CI-smoke (PR): basic smoke run included, no regressions detected on PR #3842 fix branch.
observations: Prefetching provides tokens/sec gains for conversational scenario but increases p95 under memory pressure due to extra eviction churn.
Smaller cache footprints amplify p95 tail sensitivity even when average tokens/sec remains stable — important for SLA guarantees.
Memory accounting inconsistency caused false-positive noise in nightly runs until allocator accounting fix was merged.
Regression detector false positives were mostly due to baseline mismatches across runtime releases; release-tag scoping reduces noise.
next_steps: Complete integration of the regression detector into nightly pipeline and ensure Slack messages include artifact links and baseline diffs.
Add a 'sensitivity matrix' test that sweeps cache size vs prefetch ratio for each canonical scenario and uploads a heatmap artifact.
Coordinate with runtime team to add an explicit runtime metric kv.eviction_throughput to help diagnose eviction churn impact.
Finalize CI smoke job that runs a single deterministic scenario in <10 minutes for fast feedback on PRs.
